One screen per chapter: the templates to remember and the map from what a statement says to the pattern that solves it. Use it the night before an interview or a contest; follow a link when a line no longer makes sense.

## 1 · Complexity Analysis {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-complexity]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Key facts"}
- $O$ / $\Omega$ / $\Theta$ / $o$ / $\omega$ ↔ $\le$ / $\ge$ / $=$ / $<$ / $>$ on growth rates; use the limit test (@eq-cx-limit).
- $\log^k n \prec n^\varepsilon \prec c^n$; $\log n! = \Theta(n\log n)$; $H_n = \ln n + O(1)$.
- Master theorem: compare $f(n)$ with $n^{\log_b a}$ — leaves, balanced (multiply by $\log n$), or root.
- Subtract-and-conquer: $T(n-1) + n^k \to n^{k+1}$; $aT(n-1)$ with $a > 1$ is exponential.
- Amortized: total over any sequence; aggregate, accounting, potential (@eq-cx-potential).
- Budget: about $10^8$ simple C++ operations per second, about $10^7$ in Python.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Any problem: look at $n$ and the value bounds first | Constraints → complexity | @sec-cx-p1 |
| $n \le 20$ | Enumerate subsets, $O(2^n n)$ | @sec-cx-p1-lock |
| Values up to $10^{9}$–$10^{18}$ | Formula, binary search, $O(\sqrt{x})$, $O(\log x)$ | @sec-cx-p1-kth, @sec-cx-p2-common-divisors |
| Divisors of a large number | Loop to $\sqrt x$ | @sec-cx-p2-common-divisors |
| For every $i$, iterate its multiples | Harmonic sum, $O(n \log n)$ | @sec-cx-p2-orac |
| `while` inside `for` that only moves forward or pops | Amortized $O(n)$ total | @sec-cx-p3 |
| Recursion that halves the input | Master theorem | @sec-cx-p4-pow, @sec-cx-p4-good-string |
| Recursion with overlapping subproblems | Memoise: states × work per state | @sec-cx-p4-fib |
| Recursion on a list or a skewed tree | $O(n)$ stack; convert to iteration | @sec-cx-p5 |
| Library call inside a loop | Replace by its true cost | @sec-cx-p6 |
:::

## 2 · Proof Techniques for Algorithms {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-proofs]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Loop:** invariant (initialisation, maintenance, termination) + variant for termination.
- **Recursion/DP:** strong induction on size or state order; trust the recursive calls.
- **Greedy:** exchange (swap the first difference) or stays ahead (induction on steps); always test against brute force.
- **Existence:** extremal element, or pigeonhole (more items than boxes).
- **Lower bounds:** $\lceil\log_2(\#\text{outcomes})\rceil$; adversary for exact counts ($\lceil 3n/2\rceil - 2$ min-max, $n + \lceil\log_2 n\rceil - 2$ second largest).
- **Processes:** invariant ⇒ impossibility; monovariant ⇒ termination.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal | Technique | Section |
|---|---|---|
| A loop whose correctness is not obvious | Loop invariant + variant | @sec-pf-p1 |
| Binary search that may not terminate | Variant $hi - lo$ must shrink; round `mid` correctly | @sec-pf-invariants |
| "One pass, keep a candidate" | Invariant on the processed prefix | @sec-pf-p1-majority |
| Recursive or DP solution | Strong induction on size / state order | @sec-pf-induction |
| Two-player game on a number | Brute-force table, guess pattern, prove by induction | @sec-pf-p2 |
| "Sort by some key, then take greedily" | Test against brute force; exchange or stays ahead | @sec-pf-p3 |
| "Some element with property X exists" | Extremal principle | @sec-pf-p4-peak |
| More items than possible values / residues | Pigeonhole | @sec-pf-p4-duplicate, @sec-pf-p4-modulo |
| "Can you do better?", query limits | Decision tree, adversary | @sec-pf-p5 |
| "Apply operations; can you reach the target?" | Invariant of the process | @sec-pf-p6 |
| "Does this process stop?" | Monovariant | @sec-pf-process |
:::

## 3 · Python and C++ for DSA {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-lang]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- Count / group: `Counter`, `defaultdict(list)`; C++ `unordered_map` with `custom_hash`.
- LRU: `OrderedDict.move_to_end` + `popitem(last=False)`; C++ `list::splice` + map of iterators.
- Window max: monotonic `deque` of indices.
- Max-heap in Python: push `-x`; entries `(key, tiebreak, item)`; lazy deletion by comparing with the true value.
- C++ min-heap: `priority_queue<T, vector<T>, greater<>>`; lambda comparators use `>` for a min-heap.
- Sorting: tuple keys and stability in Python, strict `<` comparators in C++; `cmp_to_key` only when the order is pairwise.
- `bisect_right(a, x)` = count of $\le x$; largest $\le x$ is index `bisect_right(a, x) - 1`; C++ `prev(s.upper_bound(x))`.
- Fast I/O: `sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()` and one `write`; `sync_with_stdio(false)`, `cin.tie(nullptr)`, `'\n'`.
- Integers: `1LL *`, `lo + (hi - lo) / 2`, `math.isqrt`, cross-multiplication, `((x % m) + m) % m`, `pow(a, p - 2, p)`.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Group, count, "have we seen it" | Hash map / `Counter` / `defaultdict` | @sec-lang-p1-anagrams |
| "Most recently used", evict the oldest | `OrderedDict`, `list` + iterator map | @sec-lang-p1-lru |
| Max or min of every window | Monotonic `deque` | @sec-lang-p1-window-max |
| Repeatedly take the largest / smallest | Heap (negate for max in Python) | @sec-lang-p2-stones |
| Merge sorted streams, $k$ best | Heap of `(key, tiebreak, item)` | @sec-lang-p2-merge |
| Delete from a heap, corrections | Lazy deletion | @sec-lang-p2-stock |
| Order decided by pairs ("concatenate") | Comparator, check strict weak ordering | @sec-lang-p3-largest |
| "Sort by …, then by …" | Tuple key, stable sort | @sec-lang-p3-frequency |
| "How many $\le x$" over a static array | Sort + `bisect_right` / `upper_bound` | @sec-lang-p4-drink |
| Largest available $\le x$, with removals | `multiset` / DSU over sorted positions | @sec-lang-p4-tickets |
| Latest version at time $t$ | Append-only sorted lists + bisect | @sec-lang-p4-timemap |
| $t \le 10^4$ tests, $10^5$+ numbers | Read all, write once | @sec-bst-p3-a |
| Tree as a parent array, $n \ge 10^5$ | Iterative order instead of recursion | @sec-lang-p5-subordinates |
| Values near $2^{31}$, squares, products | 64-bit / `__int128`, exact integer roots | @sec-lang-p6 |
| Negative numbers with `%` | Normalise the remainder | @sec-lang-p6-divisible |
| Slopes, ratios, geometry | Reduced integer pairs, cross products | @sec-lang-p6-points |
| "Modulo $10^9+7$", combinations | Factorials and Fermat inverses | @sec-lang-p6-binomial |
| Hash map on input integers (Codeforces) | `splitmix64` / XOR with a random key | @sec-lang-p7-powers |
| Pairs with equal $a_i - i$, small key range | Array indexed by value, no hashing | @sec-lang-p7-same-differences |
:::

## 4 · Testing and Debugging {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-testing]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Stress test:** brute force (from the statement) + solution + generator (tiny $n$, tiny values) + compare loop; a crash is a failure.
- **Generators:** `sample` for distinct, `shuffle` for permutations, small alphabets for strings, random parent / Prüfer / path / star for trees, tree + extra edges for connected graphs, forward edges in a random order for DAGs; one seed per test.
- **Shrink:** delete chunks, delete items, shrink values, global moves; stop when no smaller candidate fails.
- **Edge sweep:** empty, 1, 2, all equal, sorted, extremes, overflow at max size, multi-test with several cases, enumerate all small inputs.
- **Verdicts:** WA → stress + edges + overflow; WA on test 2 → reset; TLE → worst-case generators and step counts; RE → bounds, recursion depth, division by zero; ILE → flush.
- **Interactive:** solution takes `ask`; local judge validates, counts, checks; test every hidden value.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal | Technique | Section |
|---|---|---|
| An unproved greedy, comparator or update rule | Stress test against brute force with a biased value pool | @sec-test-p1 |
| Bug needs duplicates or ties to show | Small value ranges, small alphabets | @sec-test-stress |
| Input is a tree, graph, DAG or set of intervals | Structured generators, several families | @sec-test-p2 |
| Counterexample found but too long to read | Shrink with chunk deletion, value shrinking, global moves | @sec-test-p3 |
| Failure in a sequence of operations | Binary search the first wrong operation | @sec-test-debugging |
| Small input space | Enumerate all small inputs | @sec-test-edge-cases |
| Many test cases per input | Multi-test generator; reset all state | @sec-test-p4-good-subarrays |
| Products, squares, sums of $10^5$ values | Max test plus an int-range checker | @sec-test-p4 |
| TLE although random tests are fast | Worst-case generators and step counting | @sec-test-p5-consecutive |
| RE on a large tree | Path generator; iterative DFS | @sec-test-p5-kefa |
| "This is an interactive problem" | Local judge with validation and a query counter | @sec-test-p6 |
| Several correct outputs | A checker, not an output comparison | exercise 8 |
:::

## 5 · Introduction to Arrays {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-arr]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Address of `a[i]`:** `base + i * size`; scan in order, last index innermost in 2D; row-major id `i * C + j`, back with `id // C`, `id % C`.
- **Single-pass aggregate:** `state = summary(empty)`; `for x in a: state = update(state, x)`; invariant "state summarises $[0, i)$". Pairs $i < j$: use the prefix extreme, *then* add $a_j$.
- **Read/write compaction:** `w = 0; for r: if keep(a[r], a[0:w]): a[w] = a[r]; w += 1`; always `w <= r`; at most $k$ copies in sorted input: `w < k or a[r] != a[w - k]`.
- **Rotate right by $k$:** `k %= n`; reverse all, reverse $[0, k)$, reverse $[k, n)$. Many rotations: `start = (start - k) mod n`, read `a[(start + i) % n]`.
- **Carry loop:** from the least significant digit, `s = a + b + carry`, write `s % 10`, `carry = s // 10`; a final carry adds a digit.
- **Two values in one cell:** `a[i] += M * new`, read old as `a[i] % M`, new as `a[i] // M`; $M^2$ must fit.
- **Frequency array:** `cnt[x - MIN] += 1`; `less[v + 1] = less[v] + cnt[v]` gives ranks and counting sort; count the counts for "are the counts distinct".
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Answer is one summary of all cells (max, count, top-$k$, longest streak) | Single-pass aggregates | @sec-arr-p1 |
| A per-position answer needs one global fact first ("max of the others") | Two passes over running state | @sec-arr-scan, @sec-arr-p1-b |
| Best pair $i < j$ with an extreme partner ("largest $a_j - a_i$") | Prefix extreme as a running variable | @sec-arr-p1 |
| "Modify in place", keep order, remove or compact, return the new length | Read/write pointers | @sec-arr-p2 |
| Sorted input, "at most $k$ copies" | Read/write, compare with `a[w - k]` | @sec-arr-p2-b |
| Output longer than the input (duplicate, insert) in place | Read/write from the back | @sec-arr-inplace, @sec-arr-p2 |
| Rotate by $k$, cyclic shift, "two blocks swap places" | Three reversals ($k \bmod n$ first) | @sec-arr-p3 |
| Many rotations, few reads | Start offset, $(start + i) \bmod n$ | @sec-arr-p3 |
| "Is it a rotation of …", "sorted and rotated" | Windows of $aa$; count circular drops | @sec-arr-p3 |
| Number as a digit array; "add one" | Carry from the least significant end | @sec-arr-p4 |
| Index rule: $a[a[i]]$, $2i$, $i \bmod n$, $rC + c$ | Simulation and index arithmetic | @sec-arr-p4 |
| A new value per cell from old values, $O(1)$ space | Encode two values in one cell | @sec-arr-inplace, @sec-arr-p4-b |
| Values in a small range; "how many smaller"; counting sort | Frequency array + running sum | @sec-arr-p5 |
| "Are the counts distinct?", "how many values occur $k$ times?" | Frequency of frequencies | @sec-arr-p5-b |
| Values up to $10^9$ | Not a counting array: hash map or sort | @sec-hash, @sec-srt |
:::

## 6 · Prefix Sums & Difference Arrays {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-pref]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Range sum:** $P[0]=0$, $P[i+1]=P[i]+a[i]$, answer $=P[r]-P[\ell]$. $O(n+q)$.
- **Range add, read once:** $d[\ell]\mathrel{+}=v$, $d[r]\mathrel{-}=v$ with $n+1$ cells, then one prefix pass. $O(n+u)$.
- **Count subarrays by property:** key the running prefix by $p-k$ (equality), $p\!\bmod k$ (divisibility), $p$ itself (balance); seed the empty prefix. $O(n)$.
- **Rectangle sum:** $P[r_2][c_2]-P[r_1][c_2]-P[r_2][c_1]+P[r_1][c_1]$; **rectangle add** uses the mirrored four writes.
- **No inverse?** Build a suffix table and combine: `out[i] = prefix[i] (op) suffix[i]`.
- **Cuts:** $\text{left}=P[k]$, $\text{right}=\text{total}-P[k]$; scan all $k$ unless every element is non-negative.
- **Count in a range:** prefix sums of a 0/1 indicator array. **Modulo $M$:** $(P[r]-P[\ell]+M) \bmod M$.
- **Longest range with sum $k$:** map from prefix value to its *first* index; **best range sum:** $\max_j (P[j] - \min_{i<j} P[i])$.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Array never changes; many "sum of this range" questions; $n$ and $q$ both $\ge 10^5$ | Range sum queries | @sec-pref-p1 |
| **Count** subarrays with sum $=k$, divisible by $k$, equal to their length; negatives present | Prefix sums with a hash map | @sec-pref-p2 |
| Many "add $v$ to $[l,r]$" updates, and the array is read only once at the end | Difference arrays | @sec-pref-p3 |
| Grid plus rectangle sums, block averages, "largest square under budget" | Two-dimensional prefix sums | @sec-pref-p4 |
| The aggregation is XOR / product / min / max, or "everything except me" | Prefix and suffix of other operations | @sec-pref-p5 |
| Cut the array into two or three parts whose sums are equal, ordered, or balanced | Split points | @sec-pref-p6 |
| One prefix is ever live (a pivot, a running comparison) | Drop the table, keep a scalar | @sec-pref-p1-b, @sec-pref-p6-a |
| The predicate flips as you scan (duplicates, negatives, zeros) | No binary search: scan all cut points | @sec-pref-p6-a, @sec-pref-p6-b |
| "How many cells in $[\ell, r)$ have property X", many queries | Prefix counts of an indicator array | @sec-pref-def |
| Answer "modulo $10^9+7$", or sums too large for 64 bits | Prefix sums stored modulo $M$, subtract with $+M$ | @sec-pref-def |
| **Longest** / **shortest** subarray with a given sum or balance | Prefix map storing first / last index | @sec-pref-hash |
| Range adds on coordinates up to $10^9$; "maximum overlap" | Sparse difference array: sorted events, sweep | @sec-pref-diff |
| Best subarray sum, "max of $P[j] - P[i]$ with $i<j$" | Prefix sum against a running prefix minimum | @sec-pref-other |
:::

## 7 · Hashing & Counting {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-hash]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Complement lookup:** for each `x`, look up `t - x` in the seen map, *then* insert `x`. Store indices to find a pair, counts to count pairs. $O(n)$ expected.
- **Grouping by a key:** rewrite "when do two objects match?" as equality of a key — $a_i - i$, $a_i \bmod k$, a sorted tuple — then `ans += cnt[key]; cnt[key] += 1`, or $\sum \binom{c}{2}$ over the groups. $O(n)$ expected.
- **Existence and recency:** a set answers "seen before?"; a map `last[x] = i` answers "seen within $k$ steps?"; `len(set(a))` counts distinct values.
- **Voting:** for threshold $n/(k{+}1)$ keep $k$ candidates; match a seat first, else fill an empty seat, else decrement all. Verify by counting unless a winner is promised. $O(n)$ time, $O(k)$ space.
- **Membership walks:** `s = set(a)`; walk upward only from values with `x - 1` absent. $O(n)$ total.
- **Remainder map:** `last = {0: -1}`; at each `i`, look up `(pref - need) mod p`, then store `last[pref] = i`. Latest index gives the shortest window, earliest gives the longest.
- **C++ armour:** `unordered_map<long long, V, CustomHash>` with splitmix64 and a clock seed; or `map`; or sort.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Two numbers that sum to $t$", "count pairs with sum $k$", unsorted input | Complement lookup on a seen map (query, then insert) | @sec-hash-p1 |
| Rule mixes value and position ($a_j - a_i = j - i$), anagrams, equal rows, equal remainders | One key per element, then $\binom{c}{2}$ per group | @sec-hash-p2 |
| "Distinct", "contains duplicate", "same value within $k$ indices" | Set, or a map to the latest index | @sec-hash-p3 |
| A value occurs more than $n/2$ or $n/3$ times; "$O(1)$ extra space" | Voting; verify unless existence is promised | @sec-hash-p4 |
| "Consecutive values", "does $x - 1$ exist?", $O(n)$ required, unsorted | Set, and walk only from run starts | @sec-hash-p5 |
| Subarray sum divisible by $p$, shortest or longest such window | Remainder → latest (or earliest) index map | @sec-hash-p5 |
| Keys are small non-negative integers (up to about $10^6$) | Frequency array, no hashing | @sec-arr-p5 |
| Need the nearest key, the $k$-th smallest, or keys in order | `map` or sorting, not a hash table | @sec-hash-sets |
| C++ on a judge with hacks, integer keys, large $n$ | Seeded custom hash, or `map`, or sort | @sec-hash-anti |
| Input sorted (or sortable) and memory matters | Two pointers instead of a table | @sec-tp |
:::

## 8 · Two Pointers {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-tp]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Ends-squeeze:** `while lo < hi`, one test, *one* retire (the proof of @sec-tp-ends), $O(n)$ after the sort. Pairs: existence, value, extremum (@sec-tp-p1).
- **Fix-and-squeeze:** sort, outer loop over fixes, Pattern 1 on the suffix; dedup = run skips; $O(n^{k-1})$ for $k$-SUM (@sec-tp-p2, @sec-tp-fix).
- **Merge skeleton:** fingers at the smallest unprocessed heads (or the largest tails, in place); union / intersection / difference change the *emission rule* only (@sec-tp-p3, @sec-tp-merge).
- **Greedy pairing:** sort, commit the extreme, test the opposite end; prove it with one swap (@sec-tp-p4).
- **Counting:** bank $\mathit{hi} - \mathit{lo}$ per accepted step; band $=$ `count_le(r) - count_le(l - 1)`, or one sweep with two left-moving boundaries; 64-bit accumulator (@sec-tp-p5).
- **Group pointer:** $j$ jumps the chain, one settlement per run, $O(n)$ by charging (@sec-tp-p6).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Sorted (or free to sort), one pair to find / value / extremum | Opposite ends, one discard per test | @sec-tp-p1 |
| Three or more indices summing to (or nearest to) a target | Fix $k-2$, squeeze the rest | @sec-tp-p2 |
| Two sorted inputs; merge, union, intersection, difference | The merge skeleton, direction by destination | @sec-tp-p3, @sec-tp-merge |
| In-place merge, spare room only at the tail | Back-to-front, larger-tail writes | @sec-tp-p3-a, @sec-tp-merge |
| "Minimum groups, at most two per group", capacity bound | Commit the heaviest, test the lightest | @sec-tp-p4-a |
| "Pair everybody, minimise the largest pair" | Smallest with largest, both fingers move | @sec-tp-p4-b |
| "**Count** pairs with a sum above / below a bound" (after any per-index transform) | Counting squeeze, bank $\mathit{hi} - \mathit{lo}$ per step | @sec-tp-p5-a |
| "**Count** pairs with $l \le \mathit{sum} \le r$" | Band = two one-sided counts, or one sweep with two boundaries | @sec-tp-p5-b, @sec-tp-p5-c |
| Outputs or objectives phrased in blocks, runs, stretches | Group pointer, one settlement per block | @sec-tp-p6 |
| Single pair, **unsorted**, original indices wanted | Hash map — sorting would lose the indices | @sec-hash-p1-a |
| Equality / divisibility condition on pairs | Hash grouping, not fingers | @sec-hash-p2 |
| Longest / shortest / count of *subarrays* with a monotone rule | Window with a never-rewinding left bound | @sec-tp-count, @sec-sw |
| Pair counts reaching $\binom{n}{2} \approx 2\cdot10^{10}$ | Any counting form — plus a 64-bit accumulator | @sec-arr-cost |
:::

## 9 · Sliding Window {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-sw]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Fixed slide:** build the first window, then `cur += a[l+k-1] - a[l-1]`, `best = better(best, cur)`; $O(n)$; any undoable fold; also on the *complement* window (@sec-sw-p1).
- **Longest valid window (shrink-safe rule):** grow right; `while` invalid, drop `a[l]`; record `max(r - l + 1)` **after** the repair (@sec-sw-p2).
- **Shortest valid window (grow-safe rule):** grow right; `while` valid, record `min(r - l + 1)` **inside**, then drop `a[l]` (@sec-sw-p3).
- **Counting:** after the repair add `r - l + 1` (shrink-safe) or, while valid, add `n - r` per left end (grow-safe); exactly $k$ = at most $k$ minus at most $k - 1$ (@sec-sw-p4).
- **Frequency table:** `freq[v] += 1` on enter, `-= 1` and erase at zero on leave; validity is an $O(1)$ read (@sec-sw-p5).
- **Not a window:** negatives or exact sums → prefix sums + hash map; window min/max → monotone deque (@sec-sw-a5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Subarray of length exactly $k$" | Fixed-size slide (add enterer, drop leaver) | @sec-sw-p1, @sec-sw-a1 |
| Take $k$ items from the two ends / remove ends to reach a value | Window on the complement (the kept middle) | @sec-sw-p1-b, @sec-sw-p3-b |
| Longest stretch within a budget (at most $k$ zeros, sum $\le T$, at most $k$ kinds) | Longest valid window, log after the repair | @sec-sw-p2, @sec-sw-a2 |
| Shortest subarray reaching a threshold (sum $\ge$ target, contains all of a set) | Shortest valid window, log inside the repair | @sec-sw-p3, @sec-sw-a3 |
| Count subarrays with a shrink-safe rule (product $< k$, sum $\le T$) | Batch `r - l + 1` | @sec-sw-p4-a, @sec-sw-a4 |
| Count subarrays with a grow-safe rule ("at least $k$ copies") | Batch `n - r` | @sec-sw-p5-b, @sec-sw-a4 |
| Count subarrays with **exactly** $k$ (distinct values, odd numbers) | at-most-$k$ minus at-most-$(k-1)$ | @sec-sw-p4-b, @sec-sw-a4 |
| All-distinct window, or a condition on counts of values | Window with a frequency table | @sec-sw-p5 |
| Negatives, or "sum exactly $s$" | **Not a window** — prefix sums + hash map | @sec-sw-a5, @sec-pref-hash |
| Min / max of every window | **Not a running fold** — monotone deque | @sec-sw-a5 |
:::

## 10 · Sorting as a Tool {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-srt]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Sort + neighbour scan:** `b = sorted(a)`; the closest pair is some `b[i+1]-b[i]`; $O(n\log n)$ (@sec-srt-p1).
- **Multi-key order:** tuple key with negated descending fields; a C++ comparator is a strict weak ordering (never `<=`); sort indices when values must not move (@sec-srt-a2, @sec-srt-p2-a).
- **Exchange comparator:** compare what swapping two neighbours changes ($s(a)h(b)$ vs $s(b)h(a)$); cross-multiply; prove it is "compare $f(a)$ with $f(b)$" (@sec-srt-p2-b).
- **Counting sort:** `cnt[v] += 1`, emit in the required walk order; prefix sums of `cnt` give a stable version; $O(n+V)$ only while $V$ is small (@sec-srt-a3, @sec-srt-p3-a).
- **Buckets for the max gap:** width `max(1, (mx-mn)//(n-1))`, keep per-bucket min/max, answer = best seam; $O(n)$ (@sec-srt-p3-b).
- **Compression:** `rank = {v: i+1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted(set(a)))}`; $10^9$ values become $1\dots n$ (@sec-srt-p4-a).
- **Sorted counts:** `f = sorted(Counter(a).values())`; values with count $\ge f_i$ are $f_i \dots f_{m-1}$ (@sec-srt-p4-b).
- **Median / weighted median:** sort, walk to half the (weighted) count, sum deviations in 64-bit (@sec-srt-p5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Closest pair", "minimum absolute difference", two-team seam | Sort, then scan neighbours | @sec-srt-p1 |
| "Rebuild an order", sort by several fields with mixed directions | Tuple key (prove the greedy after it) | @sec-srt-p2-a |
| "Arrange pieces to maximise/minimise", order depends on two items together | Exchange argument → comparator → key | @sec-srt-p2-b |

| "Maximum successive gap" over a $10^9$ range, linear time required | Buckets + averaging bound | @sec-srt-p3-b |
| "Replace by rank", values up to $10^9$ but only order matters | Coordinate compression `sorted(set)` | @sec-srt-p4-a |
| "Every value occurs the same number of times", only counts matter | Sort the frequencies, read counts from positions | @sec-srt-p4-b |
| "Make all equal, cost $=$ total movement" | Median | @sec-srt-p5-a |
| Movement priced per unit per element | Weighted median (cumulative walk) | @sec-srt-p5-b |
:::

## 11 · Binary Search as a Tool {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-bst]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **First true:** `lo, hi = 0, n; while lo < hi: mid = (lo + hi) // 2; if P(mid): hi = mid else: lo = mid + 1; return lo` ($n$ means none). Last true of the opposite shape: first true of `not P`, minus one (@sec-bst-a1).
- **Two brackets:** `bisect_left(a, x)` $=$ #(< x), `bisect_right(a, x)` $=$ #(<= x); run of $x$ $=$ `[left, right)`; count in $[L, R]$ $=$ `right(R) - left(L)`; floor $=$ `a[right(x) - 1]` (@sec-bst-a2, @sec-bst-p1).
- **Sort once, query many:** $O(n\log n) + O(\log n)$ per query; nearest value $=$ one of the two neighbours of the insertion point (@sec-bst-a3, @sec-bst-p2).
- **Derived monotone array:** prefix sums (values $\ge 0$) or `accumulate(a, max)` (any values); fewest to reach $X$ $=$ `bisect_left(pref, X) + 1`, longest prefix all $\le K$ $=$ `bisect_right(pm, K)` (@sec-bst-a4, @sec-bst-p3).
- **Search on the answer:** binary search the value range with a monotone check, `hi` feasible; exact objective: verify at the flip; closest objective: compare `lo - 1` and `lo`, ties to the smaller (@sec-bst-a5, @sec-bst-p4).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Sorted input; "how many $< x$ / $\le x$ / $= x$ / in $[L, R]$" | Two brackets, count = difference | @sec-bst-p1, @sec-bst-a2 |
| "Positions of a value after sorting", "first and last position" | The run is `[bisect_left, bisect_right)` | @sec-bst-p1-b |
| Sign split or threshold split of a sorted array | One bracket per threshold | @sec-bst-p1-a |
| Many queries against fixed data | Sort once, one search per query | @sec-bst-a3 |
| "Closest value to $x$", "nearest tower" | Neighbours of the insertion point | @sec-bst-a3, @sec-bst-p2 |
| "The $k$ elements closest to $x$" | Search the window start by comparing its two ends | @sec-bst-p2-a |
| Two sorted (or descending) arrays, farthest valid partner | One search per element (flipped comparator) or one walk | @sec-bst-p2-b |
| Budget or target on a running total, many queries | Prefix sums (non-negative values), then search | @sec-bst-p3-a, @sec-bst-a4 |
| "Longest prefix with every element $\le k$" | Prefix maxima, no sort | @sec-bst-p3-b, @sec-bst-a4 |
| "Smallest capacity / limit such that it works" | Search on the answer with a monotone check | @sec-bst-a5 |
| "Find $x$ with exactly $x$ elements $\ge x$" | Search $x \in [0, n]$, verify at the flip | @sec-bst-p4-a |
| "Choose a cap making a sum closest to a target" | Search on the answer plus the two-candidate seam | @sec-bst-p4-b |
:::

## 12 · Sorting Algorithms {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-salgo]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Insertion** `while j >= 0 and a[j] > key: a[j+1] = a[j]; j -= 1`; $O(n + \text{inversions})$, in place, stable (@sec-salgo-a1).
- **Selection** `swap(a[i], a[argmin a[i..]])`; $\binom n2$ comparisons, $\le n-1$ swaps, not stable (@sec-salgo-a2).
- **Merge** sort the halves, merge taking the left head on ties (`L[i] <= R[j]`); $\Theta(n\log n)$ always, $O(n)$ extra, stable; bottom-up needs no recursion (@sec-salgo-a3).
- **Quicksort** random pivot; Lomuto (`a[j] <= x` grows the left region), Hoare (two fingers, middle pivot), or three-way `< == >`; expected $2n\ln n$ comparisons; recurse on the smaller side (@sec-salgo-a4).
- **Quickselect** partition, keep only the side with index $t$; expected $O(n)$ (@sec-salgo-a4-select).
- **Heap** children $2i+1, 2i+2$; sift-down swaps with the larger child; build bottom-up in $O(n)$; heapsort swaps the root to the end, $O(n\log n)$, $O(1)$ extra, not stable (@sec-salgo-a5).
- **Lower bound** $\lceil\log_2(n!)\rceil \ge \tfrac n2\log_2\tfrac n2$ comparisons, worst case and average (@sec-salgo-a6-bound).
- **Libraries** introsort = quicksort + depth limit $2\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ + heapsort + final insertion; Timsort = runs + minrun + merge stack + galloping, stable (@sec-salgo-a7, @sec-salgo-a8).
- **Patterns** count across the merge (P2), select one rank (P3), bounded heap (P4), stable sort or designed tie-break (P5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
<!-- Copied into the Cheat Sheets appendix by gen_book.py: keep it one table, no labels. -->

| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Sort without a built-in sort, $O(n\log n)$, least space" | Merge sort or heapsort by hand | @sec-salgo-p1-a |
| "Sort a linked list" (small $n$, or "insertion") | Insertion sort by relinking | @sec-salgo-p1-b |
| "Sort a linked list in $O(n\log n)$, $O(1)$ memory" | List merge sort, bottom-up | @sec-salgo-p1-c |
| "How many pairs $i<j$ with $a_i \ge a_j$" (inversions, crossings, adjacent swaps) | Count across the merge | @sec-salgo-p2-a |
| "For each $i$, how many smaller to its right" | Merge sort over indices | @sec-salgo-p2-b |
| Pairs with $a_i > 2a_j$ or another monotone predicate | Separate cross-count pass, 64-bit | @sec-salgo-p2-c |
| "The $k$-th largest/smallest", "median", once | Quickselect on the pivot's rank | @sec-salgo-p3-a |
| $k$-th smallest where rows and columns are sorted | Binary search the value, count $\le x$ | @sec-salgo-p3-b |

:::

## 13 · Linear-Time Sorting {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-lts]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Counting sort** keys in $[0, k)$: count, prefix sums ($C[v]$ = #keys $\le v$), place scanning backward with `B[--C[key]] = x`. $\Theta(n + k)$ time and space, stable (@sec-lts-a2).
- **LSD radix sort** one stable counting sort per digit, least significant first; $\Theta(d(n + b))$; for $\beta$-bit keys pick $r$-bit digits with $2^r \approx n$ (@sec-lts-a3).
- **Signed keys** offset by the minimum, or flip the sign bit, before radix sorting (@sec-lts-a3-neg).
- **MSD radix sort** for variable-length strings: counting sort on character $d$ with an "ended" bucket first, recurse into each group (@sec-lts-a3-msd).
- **Bucket sort** $n$ buckets over a known interval, insertion sort each, concatenate; expected $\Theta(n)$ for uniform keys because $\mathbb{E}[n_i^2] = 2 - 1/n$ (@sec-lts-a4).
- **Value-as-index** values in $[1, n]$: sign marking or cyclic placement, $O(1)$ extra space; guard the range (@sec-lts-a5).
- **Frequency as bucket** `buckets[count].append(item)`, scan from $n$ down (@sec-lts-p3).
- **Pigeonhole buckets** width $t + 1$: same bucket means within $t$; within $t$ means same or neighbouring bucket (@sec-lts-p5-b).
- **Decision** verify the key promise in the constraints; if there is none, use a comparison sort (@sec-lts-a6).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
<!-- Copied into the Cheat Sheets appendix by gen_book.py: keep it one table, no labels. -->

## 14 · Intervals & Sweep Line {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-int]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Convention first:** closed $[a,b]$ overlap test `a1 <= b2 and a2 <= b1`; half-open `a1 < b2 and a2 < b1`; on integers $[a,b] = [a, b+1)$. Sweep ties: half-open processes $-1$ first, closed $+1$ first (@sec-int-repr).
- **Merge:** sort by start; extend the last block with `max(out[-1].end, iv.end)` or open a new one (@sec-int-merge, @sec-int-p1-a).
- **Insert into a merged list:** copy strictly-left, absorb overlaps, copy the rest; no sort (@sec-int-p1-b).
- **Event sweep:** $(a, +w)$ and $(b, -w)$, sort with the convention's tie-break, running sum: peak, capacity check, union length, rooms $=$ peak (@sec-int-events, @sec-int-p2).
- **Pack:** sort by end; take each interval that starts at or after the last end; $k$ resources: best-fit multiset of free times (@sec-int-p3).
- **Stab:** sort by end; shoot at the end of each interval not yet hit; fewest points $=$ most disjoint intervals (@sec-int-p4-a).
- **Containment:** sort by (start asc, end desc); covered iff `end <= max_end` (@sec-int-p4-b).
- **Cover $[0,T]$:** sort by start; each round take the farthest end among intervals starting inside the covered prefix; no progress means a hole (@sec-int-p4-c).
- **Intersect:** two lists, two pointers, advance the smaller end; a family, $[\max l, \min r]$ (@sec-int-p5-a, @sec-int-p5-b).
- **Gaps:** sort by start, running reach; a start beyond `reach + 1` (integer days) opens a gap (@sec-int-p5-c).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Ranges to "merge / combine overlapping", output maximal blocks | Sort by start, running block end | @sec-int-p1-a, @sec-int-merge |
| A sorted merged list plus one new range | Three phases (left / overlap / right), or two binary searches | @sec-int-p1-b |
| "Maximum number at the same time", "peak occupancy" | Event sweep, running count, convention-aware ties | @sec-int-p2-a, @sec-int-events |
| "Capacity $C$; is it ever exceeded?", weighted loads, small coordinates | Same sweep with weights, or a difference array | @sec-int-p2-b, @sec-pref-diff |
| "Minimum number of rooms / groups / platforms" | Rooms = peak overlap (sweep, or min-heap of end times) | @sec-int-events |
| "How many intervals contain $t$?" for many $t$ | Sorted starts and ends, two binary searches | @sec-int-events, @sec-bst-p1 |
| "Most non-overlapping intervals", "fewest removals" | Sort by end, take what fits | @sec-int-p3-a, @sec-int-sched |
| "$k$ people / machines; serve the most intervals" | Sort by end, best-fit multiset of free times | @sec-int-p3-b |
| "Fewest points / arrows hitting every interval" | Sort by end, shoot at ends | @sec-int-p4-a |
| "Intervals contained in another" | Sort by (start asc, end desc), running max end | @sec-int-p4-b |
| "Fewest intervals covering $[0, T]$", or report impossible | Sort by start, extend to the farthest end, detect holes | @sec-int-p4-c |

## 15 · Partitioning & In-Place Rearrangement {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-part]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Dutch national flag:** `[< p | = p | unknown | > p]`; less → swap with `lo`, both advance; equal → `mid++`; greater → swap with `hi`, `hi--` only. $O(n)$, $O(1)$, unstable.
- **Stable partition:** read once, append to each group (or one buffer with a write cursor per group). $O(n)$ time, $O(n)$ memory.
- **Slot pattern:** a write cursor per class stepping by $2$ (stable); or two cursors on the two slot classes swapping misplaced pairs (in place).
- **Next permutation:** rightmost $a_i < a_{i+1}$; rightmost $a_j > a_i$; swap; reverse $a[i+1..)$. Previous: mirror the comparisons.
- **Rank:** $\sum c_i (n-1-i)!$ with $c_i$ the unused values below $a_i$; unrank by dividing by factorials.
- **Strict wiggle:** median $m$; three-way `[> m | = m | < m]` over cells $A(t) = (1+2t) \bmod (n \mid 1)$. Or sort and deal both halves reversed.
- **Rotation:** three reversals; juggling over $\gcd(n, k)$ cycles; block swap with $n - \gcd(n, k)$ swaps.
- **Stable in place:** partition the halves, rotate the middle block; $O(n\log n)$.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "values $< x$, then $= x$, then $> x$"; two or three distinct values, any order inside a group | Dutch national flag | @sec-part-dnf, @sec-part-p1 |
| "… and keep the relative order inside each group" | read once, write cursors into a buffer | @sec-part-stable, @sec-part-p1-a |
| an operation that splits by a threshold; minimum number of such operations | count consecutive values out of order (inverse permutation) | @sec-part-p1-b |
| "alternate positive and negative", keep order | one read pass, a write cursor per class stepping by 2 | @sec-part-props, @sec-part-p2-a |

| "next lexicographically greater arrangement" | pivot, successor, swap, reverse suffix | @sec-part-perm, @sec-part-p3-a |
| "smallest larger number with the same digits" | next permutation on the digit string, plus overflow check | @sec-part-p3-b |
| "the $k$-th permutation", "index of this permutation" | rank and unrank by factorials | @sec-part-rank |

## 16 · Index Tricks: Cyclic Sort, Marking & Permutation Cycles {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-idx]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Cyclic sort:** `while i < n: h = a[i]-1; if 0 <= h < n and a[h] != a[i]: swap(a[i], a[h]) else: i += 1`. At most $n$ swaps; exactly $n - c$ on a permutation (@sec-idx-a2, @sec-idx-p1).
- **Marking:** negate cell $|x| - 1$ for a seen bit, read with `abs`; add $n$ to cell $a_i \bmod n$ for a count, read `// n` and `% n`; restore afterwards (@sec-idx-a3, @sec-idx-p2).
- **Cycles:** one walk per cycle, $O(n)$. Minimum swaps $n - c$; parity of $n - c$ is the parity of any sorting sequence; apply a permutation in place by carrying a value round each cycle (@sec-idx-a4, @sec-idx-p3).
- **Missing values by arithmetic:** $\frac{n(n+1)}{2} - \sum a_i$ (64-bit) or XOR of the range and the array; two unknowns need sum of squares or the XOR split; $f(t) = 0 \oplus \cdots \oplus t = [t, 1, t+1, 0][t \bmod 4]$ (@sec-idx-a5, @sec-idx-p4).
- **Permutation algebra:** inverse `q[p[i]] = i`; composition `r[i] = p[q[i]]`; power along cycles with $(t + k) \bmod L$; order $=$ lcm of cycle lengths (@sec-idx-a6, @sec-idx-p5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|

## 17 · Matrices & 2D Arrays {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-mat]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Flatten:** $\text{flat}(i,j) = iC + j$, $\text{unflat}(k) = (k \div C,\, k \bmod C)$; keep `j` in the inner loop; neighbours from a clockwise direction array.
- **Spiral:** walls `top, bottom, left, right`; walk an edge, move its wall, re-test `top <= bottom` / `left <= right` before the return edges. Rings: $\min(i, j, R-1-i, C-1-j)$.
- **Diagonals:** key $i - j$ (down-right) or $i + j$ (down-left); $R + C - 1$ of each; band $s$ has rows $\max(0, s-C+1) .. \min(s, R-1)$.
- **Rotate clockwise:** `new[i][j] = M[n-1-j][i]`; in place, transpose ($i<j$ swaps) then reverse each row, or four-cycles over ring $i < \lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, $j = i..n-2-i$. Counter-clockwise: transpose then reverse the row order. Rectangle: `zip(*M[::-1])`.
- **In-place notes:** flags in row 0 / column 0 with the two saved booleans, or a new state in bit 1 read as `v & 1`; record pass first, act pass second, headers last.
- **Fix two rows:** `for top: col = 0; for bottom: col += row[bottom]; kernel(col)` — Kadane, prefix hash, or sorted set; $O(\min^2 \cdot \max)$.
- **Invariants:** $i \pm j$, $(i+j) \bmod 2$, $(j-i) \bmod n$, rotation orbits, $u = i+j$ / $v = i-j$; mind the centre when $n$ is odd.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Return the elements in spiral order"; $1\times n$ edge cases | Four walls, re-test before the return edges | @sec-mat-p1-spiral |
| "Diagonal / zig-zag order" | Band index $s = i+j$, direction by parity of $s$ | @sec-mat-p1-diag |
| "Transpose an $R\times C$ matrix" | `T[j][i] = a[i][j]` into a new $C\times R$ grid | @sec-mat-p2-transpose |
| "Rotate $90^\circ$ in place" | Transpose + reverse each row, or four-cycles | @sec-mat-p2-rotate |
| "Same after rotation / make symmetric" | Rotation orbits, fix each by majority | @sec-mat-p2-mirror |
| "Zero the row and column of every zero, $O(1)$ space" | First row and column as flags, two saved booleans | @sec-mat-p3-zeroes |
| "Update all cells simultaneously, in place" | Old state in bit 0, new state in bit 1 | @sec-mat-p3-life |
| "Number of sub-matrices summing to target" | Fix two rows + prefix-sum hash map | @sec-mat-p4-submatrix |
| "Largest rectangle sum not exceeding $k$" | Fix two rows + sorted set of prefixes | @sec-mat-p4-nolarger |
| "Largest sub-rectangle sum" | Fix two rows + Kadane | @sec-mat-a5 |
| "Sum both diagonals of a square" | $i = j$ and $i+j = n-1$, centre once if $n$ odd | @sec-mat-p5-diagsum |
| "Minimum moves of a cell on an empty grid" | Manhattan distance | @sec-mat-p5-beautiful |
| "Free cyclic shifts, then pay per change" | Wrapped diagonals $(j-i) \bmod n$ | @sec-mat-p5-shifts |
| "Adjacent cells must differ", "+1 allowed" | Checkerboard parity $(i+j) \bmod 2$ | @sec-mat-p5-artem |
| "Max / min Manhattan distance to many points" | Rotate to $u = i+j$, $v = i-j$ | @sec-mat-a6 |
:::

## 18 · Designing Array-Based Data Structures {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-ds]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Swap-with-last:** `i = pos[v]`; `a[i] = a[-1]`; `pos[a[i]] = i`; `del pos[v]`; `a.pop()`. Sample with `a[randrange(len(a))]`; duplicates make `pos` a `value -> set of slots`. Shrink a dynamic array at a quarter full, not half (@sec-ds-a1).
- **$O(1)$ snapshot:** per-cell `(version, value)` records; `snap()` returns `version++`; a write under the current version overwrites; `get(i, s)` is `bisect_right(versions, s) - 1`. To undo instead, log `(index, old value)` and pop back to a checkpoint (@sec-ds-a2).
- **Counter of counters:** `cnt[f]` for "anyone at $f$?", `levels[f]` stacks plus a `top` cursor for "pop the most frequent", count buckets in a linked list for "name the min/max key" (@sec-ds-a3).
- **Array-backed hashing:** direct address or bit array for small keys; chaining with $\alpha = n/m \le 0.75$ and re-insert-everything resizes; open addressing with tombstones and a rebuild at half full (@sec-ds-a4).
- **Lazy reset:** `clock += 1` instead of a wipe and `stamp[i] == clock` instead of a scan; `base` for "assign all", a flag for "flip all", a dirty list or a sparse set to also list the live cells; fold aggregates into `(sum, count)` (@sec-ds-a5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "$O(1)$ insert, delete *and* random element" | Packed array + `value -> slot`, swap-with-last | @sec-ds-a1, @sec-ds-p1-randset |
| "Duplicates allowed; delete any occurrence in $O(1)$" | `value -> set of slots`, evict any member | @sec-ds-p1-randcol |
| "Snapshot an array; read a past version" | Tag writes with a version; floor search per cell | @sec-ds-a2, @sec-ds-p2-snapshot |
| "Undo to a checkpoint" | Log of `(index, old value)`, pop to roll back | @sec-ds-a2-rollback |
| "Back / forward through a history" | One array, one cursor, an end marker | @sec-ds-p2-history |
| "Does some value occur exactly $f$ times?" | Count of counts `cnt[f]` | @sec-ds-a3, @sec-ds-p3-freqtracker |
| "Pop the most frequent, ties by recency" | `levels[f]` stacks + top cursor | @sec-ds-p3-freqstack |
| "All $O(1)$: min / max key by count" | Count buckets in a doubly linked list | @sec-ds-p3-allone |
| "Keys are small integers (rooms, letters, $\le 10^6$)" | Direct addressing, bit array | @sec-ds-a4, @sec-ds-p4-hotel |
| "Design a hash map from scratch" | Chaining, load factor, rehash every key | @sec-ds-p4-hashmap |
| "Design a hash set; memory proportional to $n$" | Open addressing with tombstones | @sec-ds-p4-hashset |
| "Assign $x$ to all elements" between point queries | Global base + clock, refresh on touch | @sec-ds-a5, @sec-ds-p5-assign |
| "Flip all bits", "negate all" | Lazy flag, counters kept consistent | @sec-ds-p5-bitset |
| "Clear the structure" many times; iterate members | Stamps, dirty list, or sparse set | @sec-ds-a5, @sec-ds-a5-sparse |
| "When is each original item pushed out?" | First-arrival times; answer by rank | @sec-ds-p5-recent |
| "Average over many incremental updates" | Fold into `(sum, count)`; pop the pending record | @sec-ds-p5-underground |
:::

## 19 · Counting Subarrays, Pairs and Triples: The Contribution Technique {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-cnt]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Contribution swap.** $\sum_{\text{windows}} = \sum_i (\text{charge}_i)$: for a linear statistic the charge is the cover count $(i+1)(n-i)$ (odd length: $\lceil (i+1)(n-i)/2 \rceil$); for an extremal one it is $L_i R_i$, two monotonic-stack spans measured with *opposite* tie-breaks (@sec-cnt-a1, @sec-cnt-a2).
- **Sums over pairs.** Algebra for separable terms; sort and weight rank $k$ by $2k - n + 1$ for distances; per bit $c_b(n - c_b)$ for XOR (@sec-cnt-pairsum).
- **Pairs.** Fix the right end and add `seen[complement]`, or close an equivalence class with $\binom{c}{2}$. Modular conditions key on $t \bmod k$ and look up $(-t) \bmod k$; residues $0$ and $k/2$ self-pair and must not be squared (@sec-cnt-a3, @sec-cnt-p2-songs).
- **Index and value conditions.** Rewrite until each side mentions one index: one key means a histogram, two keys mean a sweep that reads one and writes the other, no separation means a bound and a harmonic enumeration (@sec-cnt-idxval).
- **Windows with a property.** Prefix equality (`ans += cnt[p - K]`, seeded `cnt[0] = 1`) works on any integers; $\text{exactly}(K) = \text{atMost}(K) - \text{atMost}(K-1)$ only on a monotone window statistic; shape properties decompose into runs, $\sum_{\text{runs}} \binom{L+1}{2}$ (@sec-cnt-a4, @sec-cnt-p3-ones).
- **Complement.** $|U|$ minus the bad set; for two overlapping bad events $|U| - |A| - |B| + |A \cap B|$ (@sec-cnt-comp).
- **Triples.** Pivot on the index that appears in two of the three conditions. With no condition between the ends, multiply left and right counts. Otherwise the leftover is one interval $[\max(a_j - a, a_k - c), \min(a_j + a, a_k + c)]$, clamped to $[0, V]$ and answered by a subtraction on a cumulative histogram — $O(nV + n^2)$ (@sec-cnt-a5, @sec-cnt-p4-triplets).
- **Small values.** Let the value be the address: $\mathrm{cnt}[v] = v$ is a table read, and when the interesting quantity is itself a frequency, index the table by it (`how[f]`) and move the cursors lazily (@sec-cnt-p5-lucky, @sec-cnt-p5-beauty).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
Every row is the same decision — *which object do I iterate over?* — taken against a different
shape of statement.

| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Sum of `sum(arr[i..j])` over all subarrays" | Contribution swap: charge slot $i$ with $(i+1)(n-i)$ | @sec-cnt-a1, @sec-cnt-p1 |
| "Sum over all **odd-length** subarrays" | Same swap, cover count $\lceil (i+1)(n-i)/2 \rceil$ | @sec-cnt-p1-oddsum |
| "Sum of ranges / of maxima / of minima of all subarrays" | Credit the *winner*: product of two monotonic-stack spans, opposite tie-breaking | @sec-cnt-a2, @sec-cnt-p1-ranges |
| "Sum of $|a_i - a_j|$ / of products / of XORs over all pairs" | Sort and weight by rank $2k - n + 1$; expand the square; count ones per bit, $c(n-c)$ | @sec-cnt-pairsum, @sec-cnt-psum |
| "Sum of distances over same-coloured pairs of cells" | Group by colour, split into coordinates, sort each | @sec-cnt-psum-weird |
| "Count pairs with `nums[i] == nums[j]`, $i < j$" | Fix the right end and charge `seen[v]`, or close the group with $\binom{c}{2}$ | @sec-cnt-a3, @sec-cnt-p2-goodpairs |
| "Count pairs with $(t_i + t_j) \bmod k = 0$" | Residue histogram + complementary bucket; $r=0$ and $r=k/2$ self-pair | @sec-cnt-p2-songs |
| "Count pairs with $l \le a_i + a_j \le r$" | Sort; two one-sided counts with two pointers | @sec-tp |
| "Count pairs with $a_j - a_i = j - i$" | One key on both sides, $a_i - i$; histogram | @sec-cnt-idxval, @sec-hash |
| "Count pairs with $j - i = a_i + a_j$" | Two keys, $i + a_i$ and $j - a_j$; fix the right end | @sec-cnt-pidx-message |
| "Count pairs with $a_i \cdot a_j = i + j$, values distinct and $\le 2n$" | Enumerate the residue class of $j$; harmonic sum | @sec-cnt-pidx-pleasant |
| "Count subarrays with sum $= K$ (values may be negative)" | Prefix equality in a hash map, seeded `cnt[0] = 1` | @sec-cnt-a4, @sec-pref-p2-a |
| "Count subarrays divisible by $k$" | The same sweep keyed on `prefix % k` | @sec-pref-p2-b |
| "Count subarrays with **exactly** $K$ of something (non-negative)" | $\text{atMost}(K) - \text{atMost}(K-1)$, one shrinking window each | @sec-cnt-a4, @sec-cnt-p3-binsum |
| "Count substrings that are all `1`" | Split into runs, $\sum_{\text{runs}} \binom{L+1}{2}$ | @sec-cnt-p3-ones |
| "Count windows containing at least one $x$" / "both $x$ and $y$" | Complement: all windows minus the runs that avoid $x$; inclusion–exclusion for two | @sec-cnt-comp |
| "Count triples with pairwise **distinct** values" | $\binom{n}{3}$ minus the triples that repeat a value | @sec-cnt-pcomp-unequal |
| "Count pairs of objects sharing **no** attribute" | $\binom{k}{2}$ minus same-attribute pairs, plus the overlap | @sec-cnt-pcomp-ball |
| "Count increasing (or decreasing) triples $i < j < k$" | Fix the middle: smaller-left $\times$ larger-right | @sec-cnt-a5, @sec-cnt-p4-teams |
| "Count triples $(i, j, k)$ with three pairwise value conditions" | Fix the middle; the rest is one interval query on a value histogram | @sec-cnt-a5, @sec-cnt-p4-triplets |
| "Count triplets with $a == b$ where $a, b$ are XORs of the two halves" | The middle cancels: count zero-XOR windows, weight each by $k - i$ | @sec-cnt-p4-xortri |
| "$1 \le arr[i] \le 500$ and a condition like $\mathrm{cnt}[v] = v$" | Direct addressing: let the value be the address and sweep the table | @sec-cnt-a5, @sec-cnt-p5-lucky |
| "Sum of a spread of *frequencies* over all windows" | Counter of counters `how[f]` plus two cursors | @sec-cnt-p5-beauty |
| "The answer is a count of $\binom{n+1}{2}$-sized things and $n \ge 10^5$" | Any of the above — the double loop is not the answer | @sec-cnt-why |
:::

## 20 · GCD, Divisibility and Number-Theoretic Arrays {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-gcd]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **The fold and its two tables.** `g = 0; for x in a: g = gcd(g, x)` answers the gcd of the whole array. "Except position $i$" needs `pref` and `suf` because gcd has no inverse (@sec-gcd-a1).
- **The chain lemma.** Distinct gcds of subarrays ending at position $i$ form a chain of proper divisors: length $\le \lceil \log_2 V \rceil + 1$. Fold the set, not the windows (@sec-gcd-a2).
- **Residue histogram.** When only $a_i \bmod k$ matters, replace the array by $k$ counters; a $+1$ move is a bucket transfer; a rising counter is a schedule (@sec-gcd-a3, @sec-gcd-p4).
- **Harmonic sieve.** Iterate divisors, not pairs: $\sum_{d \le V} V / d \approx V \ln V$. Invert "multiple of $d$" to "exactly $d$" top-down (@sec-gcd-a4).
- **Coprime pairs and canonical keys.** $\varphi$ counts coprimes to $k$ below $k$; reducing a ratio by its gcd turns equality into a histogram bucket (@sec-gcd-a5).
- **Pigeonhole counts.** $\gcd(x, x+1) = 1$; odd parts in $[1..2n]$ are $n$ buckets; the odd count in $[l..r]$ is $(r+1)//2 - l//2$. When the input is too large to touch, one count is the answer (@sec-gcd-a6).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "GCD of the smallest and largest element" | Fold endpoints; one gcd call | @sec-gcd-p1-arrgcd |
| "Largest string that tiles both $a$ and $b$" | Fold on lengths: answer is prefix of length $\gcd(|a|,|b|)$ | @sec-gcd-p1-strgcd |
| "Count pairs with equal ratio $w / h$" | Reduce by gcd → canonical key → histogram $\sum \binom{c}{2}$ | @sec-gcd-p2-rects |
| "Split into fewest segments each with gcd $> 1$" | Running gcd; forced cut at death; greedy is provably minimal | @sec-gcd-p2-split |
| "Number of distinct GCDs of all subsequences" | Chain fold $O(n \log V)$, or sieve the value domain | @sec-gcd-p3-subseq |
| "$q$-th smallest pair gcd in sorted list" | Multiple-count sieve → top-down inversion → flatten | @sec-gcd-p3-gcdpair |
| "Balance three residue buckets by $+1$ moves" | Residue histogram; forward-only sweep | @sec-gcd-p4-balance |
| "Zero all elements mod $k$ with a rising counter" | Residue histogram as schedule; $\max_d (\mathit{cnt}[d]-1) \cdot k + d + 1$ | @sec-gcd-p4-zeromod |
| "Merge adjacent non-coprimes into their lcm" | One left-to-right stack pass; fold each factor-run into lcm | @sec-gcd-p5-merge |
| "Can $k$ product-moves make array gcd $> 1$?" ($r - l \le 10^9$) | Pigeonhole: count odds; answer YES iff odds $\le k$ | @sec-gcd-p5-parity |
| "GCD of the array except position $i$" | Prefix/suffix table (no inverse) | @sec-gcd-a1 |
| "Which gcd values are reachable by extending a subarray?" | $O(\log V)$ chain per endpoint | @sec-gcd-a2 |
| "$\varphi(n)$, count of coprimes below $n$" | Sieve Euler's totient; $1 + 2\sum\varphi$ | @sec-gcd-a5 |
| "$n + 1$ integers from $\{1, \dots, 2n\}$ contain a divisor pair" | Pigeonhole on odd parts | @sec-gcd-a6 |
:::

## 21 · MEX, Distinctness and Value-Domain Problems {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-mex]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **The presence table + pointer.** `seen = set(); m = 0; for x in a: seen.add(x); while m in seen: m += 1`. The pointer never rewinds when only inserts happen. That is the amortised-`O(n)` MEX (@sec-mex-a1, @sec-mex-a2).
- **The count table + two-level histogram.** `cnt[v]` = occurrences of `v`; `fc[c]` = how many `v` have count `c`. The second is what lets you bucket by "how often" instead of "what" (@sec-mex-a4).
- **Value-domain indexing.** When `0 <= a[i] <= n`, allocate a table of size `n+2` indexed by value. Sort becomes counting-sort; membership tests become array reads; the whole algorithm collapses to `O(n)` (@sec-mex-a6).
- **Two-pointer window with a count table.** Add at right; while the invariant breaks, remove at left. Same template drives distinctness (LC 1695), MEX-scan (@sec-mex-p5-special), and CF 1628A (@sec-mex-p3-meximum).
- **Amortised-greedy pointer on a residue or MEX walk.** CF 1294D's `ans` pointer, prefix-MEX in @sec-mex-a2, and CF 1364C's `spare_ptr` all share the shape: one integer, monotone across the run, moves only when a bucket opens.
- **Spare-pool reconstruction.** Given a target sequence of MEXes, force placements on growth, draw from a value pool (spare = values never appearing as MEX targets) on same; check "already used" before consuming a spare (@sec-mex-p3-prefix-mex).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Smallest non-negative not in the set" | Presence table + walk-up; amortised $O(n)$ | @sec-mex-a1 |
| "MEX of every prefix" | One pass, one table, one pointer that never rewinds | @sec-mex-a2 |
| "Count distinct in a sliding window" | Last-occurrence pointer + set; amortised $O(n)$ | @sec-mex-a3 |
| "Frequency of frequencies" / "bucket by count" | `fc[cnt[v]]++`; histogram of a histogram | @sec-mex-a4 |
| "Is this a permutation of $1..n$?" | Sum $= n(n+1)/2$ and distinct, or MEX $= n+1$ and in-range | @sec-mex-a5 |
| "Values bounded by $n$; index by value, not position" | Value-domain table of size $n+2$ | @sec-mex-a6 |
| "Rearrange so prefix MEXes are non-decreasing" | Sort by value; emit all copies of each before moving on | @sec-mex-p1-mexim |
| "Split into two subsets maximising $\operatorname{mex}(A) + \operatorname{mex}(B)$" | Formula $\operatorname{mex}(\ge 1) + \operatorname{mex}(\ge 2)$ on the count table | @sec-mex-p1-subset-mex |
| "$q$ queries adding any $y \equiv n \pmod{x}$; MEX after each" | Residue table + amortised greedy pointer | @sec-mex-p2-mex-max |
| "Cost to reach each MEX under decrement ops" | Walk $k = 1..n$; track spares and cnt[k] pushes | @sec-mex-p2-increments |
| "Emit MEX of shrinking window, pop from either end" | Two-pointer walk with cnt table | @sec-mex-p3-meximum |
| "Given prefix MEXes, reconstruct the array" | Force $a_i = m_{i-1}$ on growth; else pick from spare pool | @sec-mex-p3-prefix-mex |
| "Max-sum subarray with distinct elements" | Sliding window + running sum | @sec-mex-p4-erasure |
| "$q$ range distinct-queries with updates" | 26 ordered sets or segment-tree bitmask | @sec-mex-p4-dcq |

## 22 · Coordinate Compression and Offline Processing {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-coord]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **The rank map.** `rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted(set(UNIV)))}` where `UNIV` includes *every value the queries will ask*. Order/equality only; arithmetic is destroyed (@sec-coord-a1).
- **The compressed BIT.** `add(rank, delta)`, `sum(rank)` prefix, `kth(k)` descent — three walks of the `i & -i` / `i -= i & -i` ladder; $O(\log n)$ each over $n$ dense ranks (@sec-coord-a2).
- **The offline ledger.** Sort query indices, sweep data with one monotone pointer, write `ans[qi]`, print at the end. Legal iff no interleaved updates and no adaptive queries (@sec-coord-a3, @sec-coord-a4).
- **The backward replay.** Answers after $k$ forward deletions = state before the $(n-k)$-th backward insertion. Merge-only structures (block sums, DSU, nearest-survivor pointers) serve this perfectly (@sec-coord-a5).
- **The event sweep.** $+1$ at $l$, $-1$ at $r+1$; sort; charge `cur × (x - prev)` between coordinates, group deltas at shared $x$. $O(n \log n)$ regardless of universe width (@sec-coord-a6, @sec-coord-p4).
- **Touch-universe compression.** Collect the $O(k)$ or $O(n)$ coordinates/vertices/edges the answer provably lives among; compress; enumerate inside it. Rectangles: both axes. $k$-th path: the $2k$ endpoints of the $k$ lightest edges (@sec-coord-p5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "Count / sum of values $\le v$ among *earlier* elements" | Rank map + BIT prefix | @sec-coord-a1, @sec-coord-p1 |
| Values (or positions) up to $10^9$ but only $O(n)$ exist | Compress the universe, allocate by $n$ | @sec-coord-a1, @sec-coord-p1-invinfinite |
| Prefix sums up to $10^{10}$; "range sums within $[lo, hi]$" | Compress prefix values, BIT by rank | @sec-coord-p1-rangesum |
| "$q$ queries, no updates" + one shared sorted order | Sort query indices, single pointer | @sec-coord-a3, @sec-coord-p2-lequal |
| "Edges of weight $\le q$; answer per $q$" | Threshold sweep with DSU merge counts | @sec-coord-p2-pathq |
| "After each deletion/undo, report …" | Replay backwards as insertions | @sec-coord-a5, @sec-coord-p3-destroy |
| "Recover sequence from prefix-condition sums" | Right-to-left + order-statistics BIT | @sec-coord-p3-restore |
| Segment endpoints up to $10^{18}$; "exactly $k$ cover" | $+1/(r{+}1)\to-1$ events, sweep, charge runs | @sec-coord-a6, @sec-coord-p4-covered |
| Sum over pairs passing a *second* key condition | Sweep one axis, BIT the other (compressed) | @sec-coord-p4-moving |
| Rectangle union with $10^9$ coordinates | Compress both axes, mark uniform cells | @sec-coord-p5-area |
| $k$-th smallest over $O(n^2)$ pair distances | Keep $k$ lightest edges, compress to $2k$ vertices | @sec-coord-p5-kthpath |
:::

## 23 · Square Root Decomposition {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-sqrt]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **The block grid.** `B = round(sqrt(n))` blocks of $\le B$ cells; a summary per block; a query = two $O(B)$ edges + $O(n/B)$ whole-block combines; a point update = `redo(b)` in $O(B)$ (@sec-sqrt-a1, @sec-sqrt-p1).
- **The lazy tag.** Defer a whole-block op in `tag[b]`; `push(b)` before any partial read/write, `pull(b)` after; range updates become $O(\sqrt n)$ (@sec-sqrt-a2, @sec-sqrt-p2).
- **Rebuild, don't tag.** When no tag exists (modulo, arbitrary set, inserts), fix only the touched block, or buffer $\sqrt n$ mutations and flush, or split oversized blocks — three rebuild cadences for three update shapes (@sec-sqrt-a3, @sec-sqrt-p3).
- **The value/colour table.** When the statement speaks of values or colours, make *that* the axis: `add[c] += x` in $O(1)$, per-value position lists, split at $\sqrt n$ into small-by-magnitude and large-by-frequency (@sec-sqrt-a4, @sec-sqrt-p4).
- **Unbalanced costs.** Precompute the side that is expensive-to-answer and cheap-to-batch; live-compute the side that is already short. $O(n\sqrt n)$ build for $O(\sqrt n)$ (or $O(1)$ interior + $O(\sqrt n)$ fringe) queries (@sec-sqrt-a5, @sec-sqrt-p5).
- **The triage.** Updates interleaved → blocks; $O(\log n)$ monoid + tight TL → segtree; no updates + $O(1)$ window slide + no combine → Mo's, ch. 24 (@sec-sqrt-a6).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Point update **and** range query, $n, q \le 10^{5}$ | Block summaries + rebuild one block | @sec-sqrt-a1, @sec-sqrt-p1 |
| Second axis on the same data (a matrix) | Per-row blocks, or a block grid | @sec-sqrt-p1-mutable2d |
| **Range** add/assign **and** range query | Lazy block tag; push before a partial touch | @sec-sqrt-a2, @sec-sqrt-p2 |
| Update is a bitwise XOR / non-summable op | Per-block bit-counts + a mask tag | @sec-sqrt-p2-xorseg |
| Insert / delete in the middle; rank or count queries | Unrolled list of blocks + periodic split | @sec-sqrt-a3, @sec-sqrt-p3-serega |
| A summary you cannot tag (modulo, arbitrary set) | Rebuild only the touched block | @sec-sqrt-a3, @sec-sqrt-p3-childseq |
| "$x$ occurs exactly $x$ times" / "add to colour $c$" | Bucket the **value / colour** axis | @sec-sqrt-a4, @sec-sqrt-p4 |
| One operation cheap, its twin expensive | Heavy/light split at a $\sqrt n$ threshold | @sec-sqrt-a5, @sec-sqrt-p5 |
| Cost is $O(n/k)$ in a query parameter | Precompute small $k$, simulate large $k$ | @sec-sqrt-p5-arrq |
| No updates, a frequency aggregate over a range | Mo's algorithm (ch. 24), **not** blocks | @sec-sqrt-a6 |
| $O(\log n)$ associative combine, tight time limit | Segment tree / lazy segtree | @sec-sqrt-a6, @sec-seg |
:::

## 24 · Mo's Algorithm {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-mo]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **Classic Mo.** Sort by $(\lfloor\ell/B\rfloor, r)$ with $B = n/\sqrt q$; four widen/narrow loops with $O(1)$ `add`/`remove`; write `ans[id]`; total movement $O(n\sqrt q)$ (@sec-mo-a1, @sec-mo-p1).
- **Rollback Mo.** When only `add` is cheap: monotone $r$ per left-block, snapshot the aggregate + stack height, add the $\le B$ fringe, read, restore *both* scalar and table; $O(n\sqrt n)$, no deletes (@sec-mo-a2, @sec-mo-p2).
- **Mo with updates.** A third, time pointer; sort by $(\ell/B, r/B, t)$ with $B = n^{2/3}$; `apply_time` stashes the old value before overwriting and guards the window touch on `cl <= pos <= cr`; $O(n^{5/3})$ (@sec-mo-a3, @sec-mo-p3).
- **Hilbert order.** Same window, a different sort key: `hilbertOrder(\ell, r)` (64-bit, `pow` covering the grid); shorter walk in practice, no tidy proof (@sec-mo-a4, @sec-mo-p4).
- **Mo + a value structure.** Hang `ftf[f]` (or a witness set, or an `off` counter) off `freq[v]` and update *everything* in lockstep so mode / exact-$k$ / MEX / "all $=3$" read in $O(1)$ (@sec-mo-a5, @sec-mo-p5).
- **The triage.** Offline + $O(1)$ slide + no associative combine → Mo; online or answer-chained → segtree / sqrt blocks; tree paths → tree Mo (deferred) (@sec-mo-a6).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Many **offline** range queries, no updates, answer slides in $O(1)$ | Classic Mo, block order $B = n/\sqrt q$ | @sec-mo-a1, @sec-mo-p1 |
| Answer is $\sum f(x)^2\cdot$weight or a pair count over a window | One scalar $O(1)$ add/remove | @sec-mo-p1-powerful |
| "How many subarrays/pairs in $[\ell,r]$ satisfy a $k$-relation" | Frequency table over a transformed (prefix-xor) index | @sec-mo-p1-xorfav |
| Only `add` is $O(1)$; a symmetric `remove` is awkward or impossible | Rollback Mo: monotone $r$, snapshot the fringe | @sec-mo-a2, @sec-mo-p2 |
| Point **updates** interleaved, but few ("$\le m$ of them") | Mo with updates: a third, time pointer, $B = n^{2/3}$ | @sec-mo-a3, @sec-mo-p3 |
| $n, q$ large and the constant bites; you still cannot answer online fast enough | Hilbert order instead of block order | @sec-mo-a4, @sec-mo-p4 |
| The answer is a **shape** of the frequencies (mode, exact-$k$, "all $=3$") | Mo + a value structure (`ftf`, an `off` counter) | @sec-mo-a5, @sec-mo-p5 |
| Query needs a *single* witness value with a property ("a value occurring once") | Window + a maintained witness set | @sec-mo-p4-oneocc |
| Next query depends on your previous answer (adaptive / `lastans`) | **Not Mo** — segment tree / sqrt blocks | @sec-mo-a6, @sec-sqrt-a6 |
| Path or subtree queries on a tree | Tree Mo (Euler tour) — deferred to the trees volume | @sec-mo-a6 (cited) |
:::

## 25 · Multidimensional & Higher-Order Prefix Sums {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-nd]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- **2D / $d$-dim prefix (read).** Build $P$ once in $O(nm)$; a sub-rectangle is $2^d$ signed table reads in $O(1)$; pad a zero row/column so a bound at $0$ reads $0$ (@sec-nd-a1, @sec-nd-a3, @sec-nd-p1-rectsum, @sec-nd-p2-3dbox).
- **2D difference (write).** The prefix's inverse: $2^d$ corner writes per rectangle-add in $O(1)$, one final prefix materialises; size the array one larger so the exclusive far corner fits (@sec-nd-a2, @sec-nd-p2-rectadd).
- **Higher-order / AP difference.** Split a range-add into slope and intercept difference arrays; fuse their two scans into `a[i] = cb*i + cc`. A degree-$k$ polynomial add needs order $k{+}1$ (@sec-nd-a4, @sec-nd-p3-aprange, @sec-nd-p3-linear).
- **Diagonal & weighted prefix.** Choose the axis: prefix along $i-j$ / $i+j$ buckets for diagonal runs; turn a double-loop sum into $\sum (\text{multiplicity})\cdot(\text{value})$ for a weighted/contribution read (@sec-nd-a5, @sec-nd-a6, @sec-nd-p4-diag, @sec-nd-p4-rybinsk).
- **The triage.** Static, arbitrary slice → prefix table; batched adds, read once → difference array; linear-in-index adds → higher-order difference; *interleaved online* updates+queries → Fenwick / 2D BIT (@sec-ds); large offline batch with a hard answer → Mo (@sec-mo).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed grid, many "sum of this sub-rectangle" questions, no updates | 2D prefix table, $O(1)$ four-corner read | @sec-nd-a1, @sec-nd-p1, @sec-nd-p1-rectsum |
| Count $x \in [\ell,r]$ with a value property, many queries | Value-domain prefix (bucket by property, prefix the counts) | @sec-nd-a6, @sec-nd-p1-rq |
| A pile of "add $v$ to this whole rectangle", read once at the end | 2D difference array (the prefix run in reverse) | @sec-nd-a2, @sec-nd-p2-rectadd |
| 3D array / cube, "sum over this box" | $d$-dimensional prefix, $2^d$ signed corners | @sec-nd-a3, @sec-nd-p2-3dbox |
| "Add $t, t+d, t+2d,\dots$ (a line in the index) to $[\ell,r]$", batched | Second-order difference: slope array + intercept array | @sec-nd-a4, @sec-nd-p3-aprange |
| Affine range adds *then* range-sum queries | Difference rebuild + 1D prefix read, one pass | @sec-nd-a4, @sec-nd-p3-linear |
| Sum a contiguous run along a diagonal (a band, `\` or `/`) | Diagonal prefix families keyed by $i-j$ / $i+j$ | @sec-nd-a5, @sec-nd-p4-diag |
| "Every pair / every subarray, each element weighted" — a digit or multiplicity sum | Contribution: $\sum_i (\text{weight}_i)\cdot(\text{value}_i)$ | @sec-nd-a6, @sec-nd-p4-rybinsk |
| Point/rectangle updates **interleaved** with queries, needed online | *Not this chapter* — a Fenwick / 2D BIT | @sec-ds, @sec-nd-a6 |
| A `matrices` tag but the solve is DP or a segment tree (718C, 1252K, 1598E) | *Not prefixing* — check the operation before the shape | @sec-nd-pit, @sec-nd-p1 |
:::

## 163 · Introduction to Trees {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-tr]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="The six templates"}
1. **Measure.** Constant on empty. `1 +` the combination of the children. Null is $0$ for a node-count and $-1$ for an edge-height.
2. **Compare.** Both null, one null, else values and the paired children. A mirror swaps the pairing.
3. **Root path.** The state is an argument. A leaf decides. Undo a shared buffer.
4. **Parent array.** Children lists, BFS order forward, reverse for subtree sizes.
5. **Unrooted.** A degree array. A star is degree $n - 1$. The leaf count is $2 + \sum (\deg v - 2)$ over vertices of degree at least $3$.
6. **Root it.** One traversal from the vertex the question names. `dist[x] + dist[y]` is the route forced through that vertex, and it reuses an edge when the two paths overlap.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| One number per subtree: size, height, sum, perfect | Measure on the way up | @sec-tr-p1 |
| Same shape, mirror, symmetric, flip | Walk two nodes together | @sec-tr-p2 |
| Root-to-leaf sum, the paths as strings, a number read down the path | State passed down | @sec-tr-p3 |
| $p_i$, boss, manager, subtree size of a general tree | Parent array, children, BFS order | @sec-tr-p4 |
| $n - 1$ edges, and the question is a star, leaves, or an edge labelling | Degrees, no root | @sec-tr-p5 |
| Distance, a path, or a spread from one vertex, on an edge list | Root there, one traversal | @sec-tr-p6 |
| Closest ancestor with a property, subordinates, inform time | Parent array, memoised walk-up | @sec-tr-p4 |
| Label or colour the edges, or turn the tree into a star | Degrees and leaf-neighbours | @sec-tr-p5 |

"Maximum depth" of a tree given as an edge list is a BFS from the given root, not a `TreeNode` recursion. A path between two arbitrary vertices, rather than a root-to-leaf path, needs the fork of the two paths and is the lowest-common-ancestor chapter.
:::

## 164 · Tree Traversals {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-tv]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="The five templates"}
1. **Depth-first.** Emit before the children, between them, or after them. A subtree is $[\mathrm{tin}(v), \mathrm{tin}(v) + \mathrm{sz}(v))$.
2. **Level.** Snapshot the queue length. One round, one row.
3. **Level-aware.** Aggregate the row, then write. A parent sees the sibling group.
4. **Thread or splice.** Morris borrows a null pointer and gives it back. Flatten's splice is permanent and builds the preorder spine.
5. **Identity.** Preorder plus `#`, or the id of `(left id, value, right id)`. Report a duplicate when the count becomes $2$.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Return the preorder, inorder or postorder, including iteratively | Stack, or the visit point in the recursion | @sec-tv-p1 |
| Is this sequence a DFS order? | The next parent lies on the current root path | @sec-tv-p1 |
| Nested intervals, or "is $u$ an ancestor of $v$?" | Entry times; number only the vertices that must be distinct | @sec-tv-p1 |
| Average, maximum, or sum of each level | One queue round | @sec-tv-p2 |
| The input is a BFS order | Children of one parent are one increasing run | @sec-tv-p2 |
| Zigzag, odd levels, cousins, same depth and a different parent | The level as a list; two passes | @sec-tv-p3 |
| In place, $O(1)$ extra memory, flatten, two swapped BST values | A splice, or Morris | @sec-tv-p4 |
| Serialize, or identical subtrees | An order plus null markers, or a subtree id | @sec-tv-p5 |

A "level" is sometimes only a depth argument a DFS can carry. Check what the answer actually needs: a finished subtree (postorder), a whole row (a queue), or the order of positions (the DFS test).
:::

## 200 · Depth-First Search {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-df]{.cs-link}

::: {.cs-map}
| When the statement looks like this | Pattern | First move |
| --- | --- | --- |

| A sum, size or count on every subtree | Exit | Children return first. Parents with smaller indices: loop from $n$ down to $2$ |
| The $k$-th vertex under $u$, or descendants at a depth | Times | One preorder. The subtree is an interval |

## 229 · Introduction to Dynamic Programming {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-dpi]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Templates to remember"}
- Five questions: **state, transition, base cases, answer, order**; then check states × transitions.
- Linear: $dp[i] = \text{combine}(dp[i - s] \oplus w)$ over the last step.
- Include/exclude: $dp[i] = \max(dp[i-1],\ a_i + dp[i-2])$.
- Grid: $dp[r][c] = \text{combine}(dp[r-1][c],\ dp[r][c-1]) \oplus g[r][c]$, one rolling row.
- Multi-state: $dp[i][s]$ over a small state machine; a limit on a count becomes a dimension.
- Kadane with phases: extend, advance a phase, or restart.
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| "number of ways", one index, fixed step sizes | Linear recurrence | @sec-dpi-p1 |
| Partly filled columns, tiles that stick out | Linear recurrence with an extra shape state | @sec-dpi-p1-tiling |
| Take or skip, neighbours conflict | Include / exclude | @sec-dpi-p2 |
| Conflict between equal or adjacent **values** | Bucket by value, then include / exclude | @sec-dpi-p2-boredom |
| Grid, moves right/down | Grid paths | @sec-dpi-p3 |
| The previous choice restricts the next | Multi-state ($dp[i][\text{last}]$) | @sec-dpi-p4-vacation |
| Holding / not holding / cooling down | State machine | @sec-dpi-p4-cooldown |
| "At most $k$" of something | Count it in the state | @sec-dpi-p4-stock-k |
| Best subarray with a one-time twist | Kadane with phases | @sec-dpi-p5 |
| Circular array | Total minus the best non-wrapping complement | @sec-dpi-p5-circular |
:::

## 230 · One-Dimensional DP {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-od]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Five templates"}
- **Range look-back.** $dp[i] = v_i \otimes \mathrm{opt}_{j \in W(i)} dp[j]$. A sliding min or max is a deque; a range sum is a prefix sum; a calendar is one pointer per pass (@sec-od-p1).
- **Weighted selection.** Sort by end time. $dp[i] = \max(dp[i-1], w_i + dp[p(i)])$, and $p(i)$ is a binary search. Closed intervals need the predecessor to end strictly before $i$ starts (@sec-od-p2).
- **Counting under rules.** $dp[i][s] = \sum m \cdot dp[i-\ell][s']$ over legal pieces, modulo $10^9+7$. A tiny graph with a huge $n$ collapses by symmetry (@sec-od-p3).
- **Reachability.** Push the moves out of every reached index. Forward ranges with a non-decreasing min-jump table become layers. A backward move becomes BFS (@sec-od-p4).
- **Suffix and partition.** $f(i) = \mathrm{opt}(f(i+1), g_i + f(i+b_i+1))$, from the right. A cut is $dp[i] = \mathrm{opt}_j(dp[j] + c(j, i))$, with $j$ walking left and exactly $k$ blocks stored as a layer (@sec-od-p5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| The best at $i$ reads a window, a calendar, or a set the input names | Range look-back | @sec-od-p1 |
| Passes cover a stretch of days | Range look-back | @sec-od-p1-tickets |
| Sliding window of a min or a max | Range look-back, monotonic deque | @sec-od-p1-jump6 |
| Weighted intervals; taking one blocks the ones it overlaps | Weighted selection, sort by end | @sec-od-p2 |
| Count schedules of those intervals | Weighted selection, $+$ instead of max | @sec-od-p2-houses |
| Count strings or walks; a symbol, a wildcard, or a last piece has a multiplicity | Counting under rules | @sec-od-p3 |
| The same walk on a tiny graph, huge length | Counting, symmetry or a matrix | @sec-od-p3-knight |
| Reach the end, or fewest jumps, and every move is a forward range | Reachability; layers when the min-jump table is non-decreasing | @sec-od-p4-jump2 |
| The legal next move depends on the length of the last one | Reachability on $(index, k)$ | @sec-od-p4-frog |
| A choice jumps over a data-dependent number of later items | Suffix, filled right to left | @sec-od-p5-brain |
| The answer is a cut into consecutive blocks; the last block has a cost | Partition; grow the block left | @sec-od-p5-shelf |
| Exactly $d$ blocks | One layer per block | @sec-od-p5-diff |
| $W(i)$ is a sliding range and the combine is a sum | Prefix sums | @sec-od-fast |
| A move can go backward, or the dependency graph has a cycle | BFS or DFS, not an index loop | @sec-od-wrong |
:::

## 231 · Two-Dimensional Grid DP {.unnumbered .cs-chapter}

[Chapter: @sec-gd]{.cs-link}

::: {.callout-important title="Five templates"}
- **Path counting.** A forward table from the start and a backward table to the goal. Through one cell the counts multiply, and the cell itself is counted once.
- **Richer moves.** $dp[r][c] = v + \mathrm{opt}$ over a whole previous row or column. Keep the best and the second best so one cell is $O(1)$.
- **Backward and layered.** A requirement decided by the future is filled from the goal, and it is clamped at $1$. A budget of moves, time, or fuel is a layer $(t, r, c)$; layer $t + 1$ is a different array (@sec-gd-p3).
- **Two walkers.** One clock, both free coordinates. A shared cell, $r_1 = r_2$ or $c_1 = c_2$, is collected once. A round trip is two forward walks (@sec-gd-p4).
- **Shape DP.** $sq[r][c] = 1 + \min(\mathrm{up}, \mathrm{left}, \mathrm{diag})$ on a one, and the area is the square of the max. A rectangle is a histogram per row, closed by a bar of height $0$ (@sec-gd-p5).
:::

::: {.cs-map}
| Signal in the statement | Pattern | Section |
|---|---|---|
| Count paths, or test whether a cell lies on one | Path counting, forward table and backward table | @sec-gd-p1 |
| The move is anywhere in the previous row or column, and you also need the second best | Richer moves | @sec-gd-p2 |
| The start value depends on every prefix of the path | Backward DP, filled from the target | @sec-gd-p3 |
| Four directions, plus a budget of moves, time, or fuel | Layered DP; the counter is the outer loop | @sec-gd-p3-out |
| A move must go to a strictly larger value | Order by value; memoised DFS or a sort | @sec-gd-p3 |
| Two paths, and a shared cell is collected once | Two walkers on one clock | @sec-gd-p4 |
| Go there and come back, right/down then left/up | Two forward walkers, $t = r + c$ | @sec-gd-p4-cherry |
| Both agents drop one row per turn | Row clock, state $(r, c_1, c_2)$ | @sec-gd-p4-cherry2 |
| Largest or number of all-ones squares | Side at the bottom-right corner, minimum of three neighbours | @sec-gd-p5-square |
| Largest all-ones rectangle | Heights per row, histogram, monotonic stack, sentinel $0$ | @sec-gd-p5-rect |
| Four directions and nothing on the walk increases | BFS or Dijkstra, not a table | @sec-gd-p3 |
| Visit every free cell exactly once | The cell is not a state; backtracking | @sec-gd-p5 |
:::
